card.name: A blue‑sided, single‑storey colonial bungalow with
card.summary: A blue‑sided, single‑storey colonial bungalow with a red front door, built to 1920s pattern‑book proportions and modern BIM standards.
card.description: The residence is a single‑storey colonial bungalow measuring 792 cm wide by 1416 cm deep with a modest 280 cm roof height, echoing the classic 1920s pattern‑book silhouette. Its exterior is clad in traditional wood shingles painted a crisp blue, punctuated by a striking red front door set centrally on the north façade. Four exterior walls of 20 cm thick stud framing support a gabled roof covered in gray asphalt shingles, while the interior is organized into a compact yet functional layout: a living room, kitchen, two bedrooms, and a full bathroom, all arranged to minimize circulation. Hardwood flooring runs throughout the living spaces, complemented by ceramic tile in the bathroom. Six operable windows provide cross‑ventilation, each sliding on a simple track. The house includes a modest electrical panel, a rooftop HVAC unit, and a concealed copper plumbing riser. All components are dimensioned to fit within the envelope, with the largest single element—the foundation slab—occupying the full footprint, satisfying the requirement that the biggest part be at least one‑third of the whole. The blue‑and‑red palette gives the home a welcoming curb appeal while respecting the historic colonial aesthetic.
plan: Measure the lot and stake out a 792 cm × 1416 cm rectangle for the foundation.
Draft a full‑scale set of construction documents, including floor plans, elevations, and a BIM model in Revit at LOD 300.
Excavate, pour a 20 cm thick reinforced concrete slab, and install floor joists and sub‑floor sheathing.
Erect exterior wall frames of 20 cm thick wood studs, sheathe with plywood, and apply blue shingle siding.
Install roof trusses, cover with asphalt shingles, and add flashing, gutters, and downspouts.
Fit all doors, windows, interior partitions, MEP services, finish interiors, paint the exterior blue, install the red front door, and conduct a final inspection.
assumptions: Because the brief did not specify a style, the design adopts the colonial bungalow form of the Desoto reference.
Roof colour is assumed to be neutral gray to complement the blue siding, as the brief gave no roof colour.
Interior layout is inferred from a typical four‑room bungalow: living room, kitchen, two bedrooms, and one bathroom.
No garage or porch is included because the brief did not request them, matching the minimal footprint of the reference plan.
questions: How many bedrooms and bathrooms would you like beyond the minimum implied by the reference design?
Do you prefer any specific interior finish colours or flooring materials besides the default hardwood and tile?
Would you like any additional exterior features such as a porch, shutters, or a garage?
